Zabno Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Żabno, Poland

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Żabno after 1692, when town owner Łukasz Franciszek Jarand granted the community rights to establish this cemetery; by 1921, 730 Jews (29%) lived there, mostly murdered at Bełżec in 1942. The cemetery became the burial site for Rabbi Izrael Elimelech Unger (buried 1867), founder of a local Hasidic dynasty, followed by successive dynasty leaders Jakow Icchak Unger (d. ~1892) and Szaloma Dawid Unger (d. 1923). On September 15, 1942, Germans shot a group of Jews here and buried them on site. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1964, with documentation noting a final burial in 1948. Around 1990, Abraham Ladner led a cleanup and rebuilt the Unger family ohel; a 2004 Holocaust memorial was funded by Dorota Aronowitz, Genowefa Dombek, Mala Forst, and Anna Shore.
